subject: PLOT genotype frequency and genotype missing rate together

messages.author: 82933c06b1097cc4
messages.subject: PLOT genotype frequency and genotype missing rate together
parts:
I want to generate one plot with both the genotype frequency and the percentage of missing data along the linkage maps. Can any body give a suggestion?
Thank you

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PLOT genotype frequency and genotype missing rate together
parts:
geno.table returns allele frequencies; if you use scanone.output=TRUE, the result is in the form produced by scanone, and so you can plot the frequencies just as you'd plot LOD curves. The trick is to find the right columns.

Here's an example:

library(qtl)
data(fake.bc)
gt <- geno.table(fake.bc, scanone.output=TRUE)
head(gt)
# chr pos neglog10P missing AA AB
# D1M430 1 0.00 0.0000000 0.7750 0.5000000 0.5000000
# D1M318 1 9.80 0.3343524 0.7725 0.5384615 0.4615385
# D1M212 1 13.11 0.2800250 0.1100 0.4831461 0.5168539
# D1M437 1 37.11 0.5276568 0.5500 0.4611111 0.5388889
# D1M490 1 53.51 0.1717978 0.1000 0.4888889 0.5111111
# D1M15 1 79.71 0.6863369 0.1000 0.5333333 0.4666667
plot(gt, lod=3:4, col=c("slateblue", "violetred"),
bgrect="gray95", bandcol="gray85", ylim=c(0,1))
plot(gt, lod=2, col="gray70", add=TRUE)

karl

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PLOT genotype frequency and genotype missing rate together
parts:
I wrote a function a while ago that does this ... may make your life easier. It takes a cross object (class can be "f2", "bc","dh", 'riself") and a vector of your genotype names - if you haven't specified this, you can leave it blank.

For example:
data(multitrait)
plotGT(multitrait)

data(fake.f2)
plotGT(fake.f2)

plotGT<-function(cross, genotype.names=c("AA","AB","BB")){
  gt<-geno.table(cross, scanone.output=TRUE)
  if(class(cross)[1]=="f2"){
    plot(gt, lod=(which(colnames(gt) %in% genotype.names)-2), col=c("blue", "red","green"), 
         ylim=c(0,1)) 
    plot(gt, lod=which(colnames(gt) =="missing")-2, col=c("grey"), add=T)
    legend("topright", c(genotype.names,"NA"), col=c("blue", "red","green", "grey"), lty=1)
    title("segregation distortion and missing data")
  }else{
    plot(gt, lod=(which(colnames(gt) %in% genotype.names)-2), col=c("blue", "red"), 
         ylim=c(0,1)) 
    plot(gt, lod=which(colnames(gt) =="missing")-2, col=c("grey"), add=T)
    legend("topright", c(colnames(gt[5:6]),"NA"), col=c("blue", "red", "grey"), lty=1)
    title("segregation distortion and missing data")
  }
}
